quizzes.topic: Magnetic Poles, Forces and Domain Theory

questions.q: The word 'magnet' comes from the region of:
questions.explanation: Lodestone attracting iron was found in Magnesia around 600 BC.

questions.q: Magnetism in atoms arises mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Moving charges produce magnetic fields.

questions.q: Like magnetic poles:
questions.explanation: N–N and S–S repel; N–S attract.

questions.q: A magnetic material (like an iron nail) is:
options: attracted by both poles of a magnet
questions.explanation: The nail becomes an induced magnet with opposite pole facing.

questions.q: The only sure test to find whether a bar is a magnet is:
questions.explanation: Repulsion happens only between two magnets.

questions.q: A group of atoms in a material whose magnetic fields (N-poles) point in the same direction is called a:
questions.explanation: A domain may contain about 10¹⁷ atoms.

questions.q: In an unmagnetised iron bar, the domains are:
questions.explanation: Their effects cancel out.

questions.q: A material becomes magnetised when its domains:
questions.explanation: An external field aligns the domains.

questions.q: If a bar magnet is cut into two halves, each piece:
options: becomes a complete magnet with N and S poles
questions.explanation: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs (no monopoles).

questions.q: Heating a magnet strongly makes it lose magnetism because heat:
questions.explanation: Random thermal motion destroys the alignment.

questions.q: Magnetic monopoles:
options: have not been found; magnets are always dipoles
questions.explanation: Every magnet has an N-pole and an S-pole.

questions.q: The region around a magnet where it exerts a force on other magnetic poles is called:
questions.explanation: Magnetic field (B).

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic field strength is:
questions.explanation: 1 T = 1 N A⁻¹ m⁻¹.

questions.q: The direction of the magnetic field at a point is the direction of the force on a:
questions.explanation: By convention, the force on a test N-pole.

questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from:
questions.explanation: Inside the magnet they go from S to N, forming closed loops.

questions.q: Magnetic field lines are:
questions.explanation: They continue inside the magnet from S to N.

questions.q: Two magnetic field lines:
questions.explanation: A point cannot have two field directions.

questions.q: Where field lines are closer together, the magnetic field is:
questions.explanation: Spacing shows relative strength; strongest near poles.

questions.q: The magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest:
questions.explanation: Field lines are crowded at the poles.

questions.q: The pattern of a magnetic field can be plotted using:
questions.explanation: Compass needles/iron filings line up along field lines.

questions.q: The direction of field at a point on a curved field line is along the:
questions.explanation: Draw a tangent to the field line.

questions.q: When two N-poles are placed facing each other, between them there is a:
questions.explanation: Their fields cancel at the neutral zone.

questions.q: The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire forms:
questions.explanation: Direction given by the right-hand grip rule.

quizzes.topic: Induced Magnetism and Methods of Magnetisation

questions.q: A material that becomes a magnet when placed in a magnetic field is called:
questions.explanation: This is induced magnetism.

questions.q: In the stroking method, a steel bar is magnetised by:
options: rubbing one pole of a magnet along it in one direction repeatedly
questions.explanation: Domains line up with the stroking magnet.

questions.q: In the hammering method, the bar is hammered while placed:
questions.explanation: Vibration helps domains align with the field.

questions.q: Heating a magnet is mainly a method of:
questions.explanation: It misaligns the domains.

questions.q: The quickest and most common method to magnetise a material is:
options: placing it inside a coil carrying direct current (solenoid)
questions.explanation: The solenoid's field aligns domains quickly.

questions.q: A solenoid is:
questions.explanation: Its field resembles that of a bar magnet.

questions.q: A solenoid behaves like a magnet only while:
questions.explanation: No current, no field.

questions.q: An alternating current (AC) in a solenoid is useful for:
questions.explanation: Its polarity reverses each half cycle.

questions.q: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is B = μ₀nI. Here n is:
options: number of turns per unit length (N/L)
questions.explanation: n = N/L.

questions.q: A 0.5 m solenoid has 50 turns and carries 1.2 A. The field inside is about (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷):
The field inside a solenoid can be increased by:
options: increasing current or number of turns per metre
questions.explanation: B ∝ nI (and a soft iron core helps).

quizzes.topic: Temporary and Permanent Magnets and their Uses

questions.q: Magnets that lose their magnetism when the external field or current is removed are:
questions.explanation: E.g. an electromagnet.

questions.q: An electromagnet is a magnet whose field is produced by:
questions.explanation: A coil carrying current around a soft iron core.

questions.q: Materials that magnetise and demagnetise easily are called:
questions.explanation: E.g. soft iron.

questions.q: Materials that are difficult to magnetise but keep their magnetism are:
questions.explanation: E.g. steel.

questions.q: The best material for making a permanent magnet is:
questions.explanation: Steel is a hard magnetic material that retains magnetism.

questions.q: The best material for the core of an electromagnet is:
questions.explanation: It magnetises and demagnetises quickly.

questions.q: An advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet is that its:
options: strength can be varied and switched off
questions.explanation: Its strength and poles can be changed.

questions.q: A permanent magnet is preferred where:
options: a continuous electricity supply is not available
the field must be switched off
questions.explanation: It keeps its field without electricity.

questions.q: Which is a permanent magnetic material?
questions.explanation: Alnico (Al-Ni-Co alloy) is used for permanent magnets.

questions.q: Which device uses an electromagnet?
questions.explanation: Also motors, cranes, MRI and relays.

questions.q: The poles of an electromagnet can be reversed by:
questions.explanation: Current direction decides polarity.

questions.q: Materials that are strongly attracted by a magnet and retain magnetisation are:
questions.explanation: E.g. iron, cobalt and nickel.

questions.q: Which of the following is ferromagnetic?
questions.explanation: Nickel, iron and cobalt are ferromagnetic.

questions.q: Materials that are feebly (weakly) attracted by a magnet are:
questions.explanation: E.g. aluminium, tungsten, sodium, lithium.

questions.q: Materials that are slightly repelled by a magnetic field are:
questions.explanation: E.g. copper, bismuth, gold, water, glass, wood.

questions.q: In diamagnetic materials, the magnetic effects of electrons in each atom:
questions.explanation: The induced field opposes the applied field.

questions.q: Which is a non-magnetic material?
questions.explanation: Rubber, plastic, wood and copper are non-magnetic.

questions.q: Magnetic materials differ from non-magnetic materials because they:
options: respond to (are attracted by) a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Non-magnetic materials are not attracted.

questions.q: Making a region free from an external magnetic field is called:
questions.explanation: Used to protect sensitive devices.

questions.q: A sensitive instrument is shielded from external magnetic fields by keeping it in a box of:
questions.explanation: Soft iron provides an easy path that diverts field lines around the inside.

questions.q: Soft iron is used for shielding because it:
options: has high permeability so field lines pass through it instead of the inside region
questions.explanation: The field is concentrated in the iron walls.

questions.q: Magnetic shields are usually made with rounded corners because:
options: field lines find it difficult to turn sharp 90° corners
questions.explanation: As noted in the book's Science Tidbits.

questions.q: Copper is classified as:
questions.explanation: It is slightly repelled by a magnetic field.

quizzes.topic: Applications of Magnets and Earth's Magnetic Field

questions.q: Magnetic recording stores sound, pictures and data by:
options: selective magnetisation (aligning domains) of a magnetic material
questions.explanation: The tape head aligns domains according to the signal current.

questions.q: Materials commonly used in magnetic recording tapes include:
questions.explanation: Also cobalt and pure iron.

questions.q: A loudspeaker produces sound by:
options: interaction of a coil's changing field with a permanent magnet, vibrating the cone
questions.explanation: Commonly neodymium magnets are used.

questions.q: A microphone works in reverse to a speaker by converting:
questions.explanation: Moving coil in a magnetic field produces current.

questions.q: Magnetic door locks used at emergency exits work by:
options: an electromagnet attracting a metal plate while current flows
questions.explanation: Switching off current releases the door.

questions.q: The Earth's magnetic field is mainly caused by:
options: electric currents in the molten iron core (dynamo effect)
questions.explanation: Motion of charges in the liquid outer core.

questions.q: The Earth's magnetic field resembles the field of a:
questions.explanation: Distorted by the solar wind on the Sun-side.

questions.q: The Earth's magnetic field protects life from:
options: harmful cosmic rays and charged particles from the Sun
questions.explanation: It acts as a protective shield.

questions.q: According to the book, the Earth's magnetic axis is inclined to its geographical axis by about:
questions.explanation: So a compass does not point exactly to geographic north.

questions.q: Auroras (polar lights) are formed when:
options: charged particles from the Sun ionise air near the poles
questions.explanation: Earth's field guides particles towards the poles.

questions.q: Earth's magnetic field intensity:
options: is very high at the equator
is very low at the poles
questions.explanation: It is generally stronger near the poles.

questions.q: Pigeons and migratory birds navigate using:
questions.explanation: Iron crystals / magnetically sensitive molecules help them sense direction.

questions.q: If a bar magnet is cut in half it will become:
questions.explanation: Each half is a complete but smaller (weaker) magnet with N and S poles.

questions.q: Which one is the quickest method to magnetize a material?
options: putting inside a current carrying coil
questions.explanation: A solenoid's field aligns domains almost instantly.

questions.q: Earth's magnetic field intensity is:
questions.explanation: It is not uniform over the Earth.

questions.q: The cause of the Earth's magnetic field is:
options: motion of ions in the core
questions.explanation: Moving charges in the molten core (dynamo effect).

questions.q: Material which is the best one for making a permanent magnet:
questions.explanation: Steel retains magnetism (hard magnetic material).

questions.q: Material which is the best one for making an electromagnet:
questions.explanation: Soft iron magnetises and demagnetises easily.

questions.q: A sensitive magnetic material is to be shielded from the external magnetic field. It should be kept inside a box of:
questions.explanation: Soft iron diverts field lines around the inside.

questions.q: Magnetic field lines:
questions.explanation: They form closed loops (N to S outside, S to N inside).

questions.q: When two wires carrying current in the same direction are placed parallel near each other, due to the magnetic field produced by each wire they:
options: have no effect on each other
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract.

questions.q: Which of the following material is ferromagnetic?
questions.explanation: Nickel, iron and cobalt are ferromagnetic.
